title: Junkers Ju 52/3m g4e (IL-2)

sources.title: JoyPro cockpit catalog (from the IL-2 and real aircraft manuals)

intro: The Ju 52/3m was a German three-engined transport plane. Two pilots sit side by side with a throttle quadrant between the seats. With fixed-pitch propellers and manual mixture the power is read from the RPM gauges, and braking is done through the throttles.

areas.name: Instrument panel
areas.text: The flight instruments and the engine gauges are in front of the pilots.

panels.name: Instrument panel
panels.text: This is the main panel. It holds the flight instruments and the gauges of the three BMW 132 engines.
panels.context: The pilots read the power of each engine from the RPM gauges.

controls.name: Airspeed indicator
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the plane moves through the air. The scale is in kilometres per hour (km/h).
controls.context: The pilot watches it all the time. Too slow and the wings stop carrying the plane; too fast and the plane can be damaged. It matters most at take-off and landing.

controls.name: Altimeter
controls.text: This dial shows how high the plane is, measured from the air pressure. The needles work like the hands of a clock, one for the hundreds and one for the thousands of metres.
controls.context: The pilot checks it to stay clear of the ground and to hold the height the mission needs.

controls.name: Variometer (climb and descent indicator)
controls.text: This dial shows how fast the plane climbs or sinks.
controls.context: The pilot watches it to hold a steady climb or descent.

controls.name: Turn and slip indicator
controls.text: This instrument has a needle that shows how fast the plane turns and a ball that shows whether it skids sideways. The pilot keeps the ball in the middle with the rudder.
controls.context: It is one of the basic flight instruments, used in clouds and for turning.

controls.name: Compass
controls.text: This is the magnetic compass. It shows the direction the plane is heading, like a hiking compass.
controls.context: The pilot uses it to hold a course.

controls.name: Tachometers (three engines)
controls.text: These dials show how fast each of the three engines turns, in revolutions per minute (RPM).
controls.context: With fixed-pitch propellers the pilot reads the power of each engine from the RPM.

controls.name: Boost gauges
controls.text: These gauges show the boost of each engine, the pressure with which the supercharger pushes air into the engine. More boost means more power.
controls.context: The throttle levers set the boost. The pilot compares the engines to keep them in step.

controls.name: Oil gauges on the nacelles
controls.text: These gauges for the wing engines' fuel and oil sit on the engine housings (nacelles) outside the cockpit and are read through the side windows.
controls.context: The pilot or co-pilot reads them through the side windows.

areas.name: Throttle quadrant
areas.text: The three throttle levers and the mixture levers sit between the seats.

panels.name: Throttle quadrant
panels.text: This is the quadrant between the two seats with the three throttle levers and the mixture levers.
panels.context: The pilots use the throttles to brake on the ground: the catalog says in IL-2 a throttle below 20 per cent applies the brakes.

controls.name: Left engine throttle
controls.text: This lever makes the left engine stronger or weaker. The catalog says that in IL-2 below 20 per cent the lever also applies the left wheel brake.
controls.context: The three throttle levers sit between the two pilots' seats.

controls.name: Centre engine throttle
controls.text: This lever makes the centre engine (in the nose) stronger or weaker. The catalog says that in IL-2 below 20 per cent the lever applies both wheel brakes.
controls.context: The Ju 52 brakes through the throttles, which is unusual.

controls.name: Right engine throttle
controls.text: This lever makes the right engine stronger or weaker. The catalog says that in IL-2 below 20 per cent the lever also applies the right wheel brake.
controls.context: Moving the left and right levers apart steers the plane on the ground.

controls.name: Mixture levers
controls.text: These levers set how much fuel goes into the air of the engines, the mixture. The pilot leans them out as the plane climbs because the air gets thinner.
controls.context: They sit with the throttles on the Ju 52 quadrant.

areas.name: Stabilizer and flaps
areas.text: The large handwheel and the flap control are at the side.

panels.name: Stabilizer and flap controls
panels.text: This is a large handwheel for the stabilizer trim and the flap control. They are linked, so the stabilizer moves when the flaps do.
panels.context: The pilot uses them for take-off and landing.

controls.name: Stabilizer handwheel
controls.text: This large handwheel trims the stabilizer, the small wing at the tail. Trim is a small adjustment so the plane flies level without the pilot holding the controls.
controls.context: On the Ju 52 it is linked with the flaps.

controls.name: Flap control
controls.text: This control raises and lowers the flaps. Flaps are parts of the wing that slide out to give more lift at low speed.
controls.context: The pilot lowers them for take-off and landing and raises them in normal flight.

areas.name: Control column and throttle
areas.text: These are the controls on the pilot's stick or yoke and on the left-hand throttle side that JoyPro can assign to a joystick or throttle.

panels.name: Control column and yoke
panels.text: This is the control column with its yoke or wheel and the buttons on it.
panels.context: The pilot flies with it; on the bombers the bomb release is on it.

controls.name: Control wheel
controls.text: This is the control column with a wheel or yoke. Pushing and pulling it tilts the plane's nose down and up, turning the wheel rolls the plane. In the game: pitch: Pitch; roll: Roll.
controls.context: It is the pilot's main flight control. On the larger planes it replaces the stick.

panels.name: Throttle quadrant controls
panels.text: These are the three throttle levers and the mixture levers between the pilots' seats, and the stabilizer handwheel beside the pilot.
panels.context: The pilot sets engine power with them and brakes on the ground through the throttles.

controls.name: Left engine throttle
controls.text: This is the throttle of the left engine. It makes that engine stronger or weaker. In the game: axis: Left engine; below 20%: left brake.
controls.context: On a twin-engined plane the pilot moves both throttles together for straight flight and one at a time to turn on the ground.

controls.name: Centre engine throttle
controls.text: This is the throttle, the lever that makes the engine stronger or weaker, like the gas pedal of a car. In the game: axis: Centre engine; below 20%: both brakes.
controls.context: The pilot works it with the left hand: forward for take-off and fighting, back for landing.

controls.name: Right engine throttle
controls.text: This is the throttle of the right engine. It makes that engine stronger or weaker. In the game: axis: Right engine; below 20%: right brake.
controls.context: Holding one throttle back while the other stays open helps to steer on the ground and to fly straight when the engines pull unevenly.

controls.name: Mixture control
controls.text: This lever sets the mixture, how much fuel goes into the engine's air. Moving it leans the mixture, which means less fuel for the air. In the game: axis: Lean the mixture above 1 km.
controls.context: The pilot leans the engine as the plane climbs, because the air gets thinner.

controls.name: Stabilizer handwheel
controls.text: This handwheel trims the plane. Trim is a small adjustment so the plane flies level without the pilot holding the controls. In the game: up: Stabilizer nose down; down: Stabilizer nose up.
controls.context: The pilot turns it after take-off and when speed or load changes.
